Lemma 7.1, Lemma 8.6: Lem $D_F\in (0,1)$ properties of $D_F$
nodes.statement:
If $\mathbb{E}[W\log W]<\log b$ and $\mathbb{E}[W^t]<\infty$ for all $t>0$, then 
 $
 D_F\in (0,1).
 $

For $1/2<\beta<1$, we have 
\[
 D_F=1 -   \inf_{1/2\le t\le 1} \frac{\log  \mathbb{E}[b^{1-t}W^{2t}]}{ t \log b} = \frac{ 2\psi(\beta)}{\log b}. 
\]

nodes.name: Proposition 1.11: Prop upper bound of $\dim_F(\mu_\infty)$
nodes.statement:
Assume that $\mathbb{E}[W\log W]<\log b$ and $\mathbb{E}[W^t]<\infty$ for all $t>0$.   Then  almost surely on $\{\mu_\infty\ne 0\}$,   for any $\varepsilon>0$, there exists some subsequence $(n_k)$  depending on $\varepsilon$,  such that 
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty} b^{\frac{n_k (D_F+\varepsilon)}{2}} |\widehat{\mu}_\infty(b^{n_k})| =  \infty. 
\]

nodes.name: Lemma 9.14, Lemma 9.15
nodes.statement:
Let $(X_n)_{n\geq 1}$  and $X_\infty$ be  complex random variables on some probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$. Assume that  $E\in\mathcal{F} $ satisfies $\mathbb{P}(E)=\mathbb{P}(X_\infty\neq 0)\in (0,1)$ and $X_n=0$ on $E^c$ for any $n\geq 1$ . 
If 
\[
X_n\xrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty]{d} X_\infty,
\]
then the following conditioned convergence in distribution holds:
\[
\mathcal{L}(X_n\mid E)\xrightarrow[]{n\rightarrow\infty} \mathcal{L}(X_\infty|X_\infty\neq 0).
\]

Let $(X_n)_{n\geq 1}$ be a sequence of complex random variables  converging in distribution to a  random variable $X_\infty$ with $\mathbb{P}(X_\infty\neq 0)=1$, then for any positive increasing sequence $(a_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ with $\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} a_n=\infty$, we have
\[
a_n|X_n|\xrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty ]{\text{in probability}}  \infty.
\]
That is, for any $M>0$, 
\[
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} \mathbb{P}(a_n|X_n|>M)=1.
\]

nodes.name: Proposition 1.12, Proposition 9.1, Proposition 9.2, Proposition 9.4: Prop weak convergence of the re…
nodes.statement:
Assume that $\mathbb{E}[W\log W]<\log b$ and $\mathbb{E}[W^t]<\infty$ for all $t>0$.  We have the following convergences in distribution  under $\mathbb{P}^* = \mathbb{P}(\cdot | \mu_\infty\ne 0)$:
\begin{itemize}
\item Squared sub-critical regime: if $\mathbb{E}[ W^{(2)} \log W^{(2)}] < \log b$ and $b\ge 3$, then 
\[
b^{\frac{nD_F}{2}} \cdot  \widehat{\mu}_\infty(b^n)  \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{\quad d \quad }      \sqrt{ \mathbb{E}[|\widehat{\mu}_\infty(1)|^2] \cdot  \mathscr{M}_\infty(W^{(2)})} \cdot \mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{C}}(0,1),
\]
where $\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{C}}(0,1)$ is  independent of $\mathscr{M}_\infty(W^{(2)})$ and $\mathbb{E}[|\widehat{\mu}_\infty(1)|^2]\in (0,\infty) $ is given in (eqn-mu-s-square-s=1). 
\item  Squared critical regime:  if $\mathbb{E}[ W^{(2)} \log W^{(2)}]  = \log b$ and $b \ge 3$, then 
\[
n^{\frac{1}{4}} \cdot b^{\frac{nD_F}{2}} \cdot  \widehat{\mu}_\infty(b^n)  \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{\quad d \quad }      \sqrt{ \mathbb{E}[|\widehat{\mu}_\infty(1)|^2] \cdot  \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi \sigma^2}}  \mathscr{D}_\infty(W^{(2)})} \cdot \mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{C}}(0,1),
\]
where $\mathscr{D}_\infty(W^{(2)})$ is the a.s. limit of the derivative martingale of BRW,  coming from the Seneta-Heyde norming limit of the $\mathscr{M}_n(W^{(2)})$  proved in [Aideon-Shi] as follows: 
\[
 \sqrt{n} \cdot  \mathscr{M}_n(W^{(2)}) \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{\text{in probability}} \mathscr{D}_\infty(W^{(2)}) \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi \sigma^2}} 
\]
   with $\sigma^2\in(0,\infty)$ given in (def-BRW-var) and  $\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{C}}(0,1)$  independent of $\mathscr{D}_\infty(W^{(2)})$.
   \item Squared super-critical regime:  if $\mathbb{E}[ W^{(2)} \log W^{(2)}] > \log b$ and $\log W$ is non-lattice, then there exists  a unique constant $\beta\in (1/2,1)$ depending only on $W$ (see (def-beta)), such that  
 \begin{align*}
b^{\frac{n D_F}{2}}n^{\frac{3}{2}\beta} \widehat{\mu}_{\infty}\left(b^{n}\right)\xrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty]{d}  \mathscr{D}_\infty(W^{(2)})^\beta \sum_{x \in \mathcal{Z}_\infty} e^{-\beta x}\widehat{\mu}^{(x)}_\infty(1),
 \end{align*}
 where $\mathcal{Z}_\infty$ is a  decorated Poisson point process  (see  (eqn-z-infinity-s)), given $\mathcal{Z}_\infty$, $\{\widehat{\mu}^{(x)}_\infty(1)\}_{x\in \mathcal{Z}_\infty}$ are i.i.d. copies of $\widehat{\mu}_\infty(1)$,  and $\mathscr{D}_\infty(W^{(2)})$ is independent of $(\mathcal{Z}_\infty, \{\widehat{\mu}^{(x)}_\infty(1)\}_{x\in \mathcal{Z}_\infty})$.  Moreover, the real part of $ \sum_{x \in \mathcal{Z}_\infty} e^{-\beta x}\widehat{\mu}^{(x)}_\infty(1)$ has a $\frac{1}{\beta}$-stable law. 
\end{itemize}

If  $W$  is in the squared sub-critical regime, 
then for $b \ge 3$, 
$$
b^{\frac{nD_F}{2}}  \cdot \widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(b^n)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{d} \sqrt{\varrho\cdot \mathscr{M}_\infty(W^{(2)})}\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{C}}(0,1),
$$
where $\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{C}}(0,1)$ is independent of $\mathscr{M}_\infty(W^{(2)})$. While for $b = 2$, 
\[
2^{\frac{nD_F}{2}}  \cdot  \Big[   \sqrt{ \frac{\varrho}{\varrho+\varpi}} \mathrm{Re} \big(\widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(2^n)\big) + i  \sqrt{ \frac{\varrho}{\varrho-\varpi}} \mathrm{Im} \big(\widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(2^n)\big) \Big]   \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{d} \sqrt{\varrho\cdot \mathscr{M}_\infty(W^{(2)})}\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{C}}(0,1).
\]

If $W$  is in the squared critical regime, 
 then for $b \ge 3$, 
$$
n^{\frac{1}{4}} b^{\frac{n D_F}{2}} \widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(b^n)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{d} \sqrt{\varrho\cdot \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi \sigma^2}}\mathscr{D}_\infty(W^{(2)})}\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{C}}(0,1),
$$
where  $\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{C}}(0,1)$ is independent of $\mathscr{D}_\infty(W^{(2)})$. While for $b=2$,
\[ 
n^{\frac{1}{4}} 2^{\frac{nD_F}{2}}  \cdot  \Big[   \sqrt{ \frac{\varrho}{\varrho+\varpi}} \mathrm{Re} \big(\widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(2^n)\big) + i  \sqrt{ \frac{\varrho}{\varrho-\varpi}} \mathrm{Im} \big(\widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(2^n)\big) \Big]   \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{d}  \sqrt{\varrho\cdot \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi \sigma^2}}\mathscr{D}_\infty(W^{(2)})}\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{C}}(0,1).
\]

If $W$  is in the squared sup-critical regime such that $\log W$ is non-lattice, then 
 \begin{align*}
   b^{\frac{ n \cdot D_F}{2} }n^{\frac{3}{2}\beta} \widehat{\mu}_{\infty}\left(b^{n}\right)\xrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty]{d} \mathscr{D}_\infty(W^{(2)})^\beta\sum_{i\in \mathbb{N}} e^{-\beta x_i}\widehat{\mu}^{(i)}_\infty(1),
 \end{align*}
 where $(x_i)_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$ is the  point process  $\mathcal{Z}_\infty$ in (eqn-z-infinity-s),  $\{\widehat{\mu}^{(i)}_\infty(1)\}_{i\in \mathbb{N}}$ are i.i.d. copies of $\widehat{\mu}_\infty(1)$  independent of $\mathcal{Z}_\infty$, and the random variable   $\mathscr{D}_\infty(W^{(2)})$ is independent of   $(\mathcal{Z}_\infty, \{\widehat{\mu}^{(i)}_\infty(1)\}_{i\in \mathbb{N}})$. 
Moreover, the limit is non trivial and  the random variable 
\[
\sum_{i\in \mathbb{N}} e^{-\beta x_i} \mathrm{Re} (\widehat{\mu}^{(i)}_\infty(1))
\]
has a $\frac{1}{\beta}$-stable law.  In particular, 
\begin{align}
\mathbb{P}^*  \Big( \mathscr{D}_\infty(W^{(2)})^\beta\Big| \sum_{i\in \mathbb{N}} e^{-\beta x_i}  \widehat{\mu}^{(i)}_\infty(1)\Big|=0\Big) =0.  
\end{align}

nodes.name: Lemma 9.5, Lemma 9.6, Lemma 9.7, Lemma 9.8, Lemma 9.9, Lemma 9.10, Lemma 9.11, Lemma 9.12, Lemma 9.1…
nodes.statement:
Fix $n\in\mathbb{N}$, we have  
\begin{align} 
 \widehat{\mu}_{\infty}\left(b^n\right)\stackrel{d}{=}\frac{1}{b^n}\sum_{|u|=n}  \prod_{j=0}^{n} W(u|_j)  \cdot \widehat{\mu}_{\infty}^{(u)}(1),
\end{align}
where $\{\widehat{\mu}_{\infty}^{(u)}(1):|u|=n\}$ are i.i.d. copies of $\widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(1)$ which are all independent of the sigma-algebra $\mathscr{F}_{n}=\sigma\{W(u): 1\leq |u|\leq n\}$.

Assume that $W$ is in the squared sub-critical or squared critical regime.  Then for any $s\in\mathbb{N}$, one has
\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}[|\widehat{\mu}_\infty(s)|^2]=\frac{\mathbb{E}[\mathring{W}^2]}{b}\sum_{m=1}^\infty \Big(\frac{\mathbb{E}[W^2]}{b}\Big)^{m-1}\Big|\frac{e^{i2\pi sb^{-m}}-1}{2\pi s b^{-m}}\Big|^2
\end{align}
and 
\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}\left[\widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(s)^2\right] = \frac{\mathbb{E}[\mathring{W}^2]}{b}\sum_{m=1}^{+\infty} \Big(\frac{ \mathbb{E}[W^2]}{b}\Big)^{m-1}  \cdot  \frac{1}{b^m}\sum_{|u|=m}\Big(\frac{e^{i 2 \pi s \cdot b^{-m}}-1}{i 2 \pi s  b^{-m}}\Big)^2 e^{i 4\pi s\, t_u},
\end{align}
where  $t_u:=\sum_{j=1}^{|u|} \frac{u_j}{b^j}$ is  the left endpoint of the interval $I_u$.

Assume that $W$ is in the squared sub-critical or squared critical regime. Then 
\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}[|\widehat{\mu}_\infty(1)|^2]=\varrho. 
\end{align}
Moreover, for  $b \ge 3$, 
\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}\left[(\widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(1))^2\right] =0
\end{align}
and if $b = 2$, then 
\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}\left[(\widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(1))^2\right] =  \varpi = - \frac{2 \mathbb{E}[\mathring{W}^2]}{\pi^2}. 
\end{align}

Assume that $b \ge 3$. If  $W$ is in the squared sub-critical regime or squared critical regime, then 
\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}\Big[ b^{n D_F}|\widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(b^n)|^2 \big| \mathscr{F}_{n}\Big] =\varrho\mathscr{M}_{n}(W^{(2)}), 
\end{align}
where $\mathscr{M}_{n}(W^{(2)})$ is  defined as in (eqn-def-mnab).  Moreover,  
\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}\Big[b^{n D_F}(\widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(b^n))^2 \big| \mathscr{F}_{n}\Big] =0.
\end{align}
 Hence, conditioned on $\mathscr{F}_{n}$,   the complex random variable $b^{\frac{n D_F}{2}}\cdot \widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(b^n)$ has a covariance matrix given by 
\begin{align}
\mathrm{Cov}\Big[b^{\frac{n D_F}{2}}\cdot \widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(b^n)\big| \mathscr{F}_{n}\Big]=\varrho\mathscr{M}_{n}(W^{(2)})
\begin{pmatrix}
1/2&0\\
0&1/2\\
\end{pmatrix}.
\end{align}
In particular, 
\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}\big[b^{ n D_F}|\widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(b^n)|^2 \big] =\varrho \text{\, and \,} \mathbb{E}\big[ b^{n D_F}(\widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(b^n))^2 \big] =0
\end{align}
and
\[
\mathrm{Cov}\big[b^{\frac{n D_F}{2}}\cdot \widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(b^n)\big]= \varrho \begin{pmatrix}
1/2&0\\
0&1/2\\
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Assume $b  = 2$. If  $W$ is in the squared sub-critical regime or squared critical regime, then  conditioned on $\mathscr{F}_{n}$,   the complex random variable $2^{\frac{n D_F}{2}}\cdot \widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(2^n)$ has a covariance matrix given by 
\[
\mathrm{Cov}\Big[2^{\frac{n D_F}{2}}\cdot \widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(2^n)\big| \mathscr{F}_{n}\Big]=\frac{\mathscr{M}_{n}(W^{(2)})}{2}
\begin{pmatrix}
\varrho+\varpi&0\\
0&\varrho-\varpi\\
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
In other words, 
\[
\mathrm{Cov}\Bigg[2^{\frac{nD_F}{2}}  \cdot  \Big[   \sqrt{ \frac{\varrho}{\varrho+\varpi}} \mathrm{Re} \big(\widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(2^n)\big) + i  \sqrt{ \frac{\varrho}{\varrho-\varpi}} \mathrm{Im} \big(\widehat{\mu}_{\infty}(2^n)\big) \Big] \Big| \mathscr{F}_n  \Bigg] = \varrho\mathscr{M}_{n}(W^{(2)})
\begin{pmatrix}
1/2&0\\
0&1/2\\
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

For any $\varepsilon>0$,  we have 
\[
\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty} \sum_{|u|=n} Y(u)\sigma\Big(\frac{\varepsilon}{Y_u}\Big)=0 \quad \text{a.s}.
\]

For any $\varepsilon> 0$, we have 
\[
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} \sum_{|u|=n} n^{1/2}Y(u)\sigma\Big(\frac{\varepsilon}{n^{1/2}Y(u)}\Big)=0 \quad \text{in probability},
\]
where $\sigma(x)$ is defined in (eqn-CLT-sigma).

There exists  $p\in (1/\beta,2]$ such that  for all $\gamma \in (0, \frac{1}{\beta p})$, we have
\[
0< \mathbb{E}[|\widehat{\mu}_\infty(1)|^p]<\infty \text{\, and \,} 
\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}^+}\mathbb{E}\Big[\big| b^{\frac{n D_F}{2}}   n^{\frac{3}{2}\beta} \widehat{\mu}_{\infty}\left(b^n\right)  \big|^{p\gamma}\Big]<\infty. 
\]

Let $p\in (1/\beta, 2]$ be taken as in Lemma 9.12. For an arbitrary partition of $\mathbb{N}$: 
\[
\mathbb{N} = \bigsqcup_{k=1}^\infty P_k \quad \text{with $P_k$ not necessarily finite}, 
\]
we may define the  martingale limits  (in the sense of $L^p (\mathbb{P}(\cdot | \mathcal{Z}_\infty))$-convergence)
\begin{align}
S(P_k): = \lim_{N\to\infty}\sum_{ i \in P_k \cap [1, N]} e^{-\beta x_i}   \mathrm{Re} (\widehat{\mu}^{(i)}_\infty(1))
\end{align}
and obtain the almost sure equality under $\mathbb{P}(\cdot |\mathcal{Z}_\infty)$ 
\[
\lim_{N\to\infty}\sum_{i=1}^N e^{-\beta x_i}   \mathrm{Re} (\widehat{\mu}^{(i)}_\infty(1))   =  \lim_{L\to\infty} \sum_{k=1}^L  S(P_k). 
\]

nodes.name: Proposition 1.10, Proposition 8.1: Prop Prop lower bound of $\dim_F(\mu_\infty)$
nodes.statement:
If $\mathbb{E}[W\log W]<\log b$ and $\mathbb{E}[W^t]<\infty$ for all $t>0$,   then  almost surely, 
\[
\tau_c(\mu_\infty) \ge \alpha_c \ge \frac{D_F}{2}, 
\]
and hence, almost surely on $\{\mu_\infty \ne 0\}$, 
\[
\dim_F(\mu_\infty) \ge D_F.
\]

We have
$
\alpha_c \ge \frac{ D_F}{2}.
$

nodes.name: Theorem 1.4, Theorem 11.1: Polynomial Rajchman property…
nodes.statement:
Assume that $\mathbb{E}[W\log W]<\log b$ and $\mathbb{E}[W^{1+\delta}]<\infty$ for some $\delta>0$. Then almost surely on $\{\mu_\infty\ne 0\}$, we have $\dim_F(\mu_\infty)>0$. In other words,  $\mu_\infty$ has  polynomial Rajchman property.

Let $\nu$ be a  Borel probability measure on $[0,1]$ with 
$
\dim_F(\nu)>0.
$
Assume that $W\in L^{1+\delta}(\mathbb{P})$ for a positive $\delta>0$ and 
\begin{align}
 \frac{\mathbb{E}[W\log W]}{\log b} < \lim_{p\to 1^{+}} \underline{\dim}_{p}(\nu). 
 \end{align}
 Then the random  measure  $Q\nu$ is non-degenerate and   almost surely on $\{Q\nu\ne 0\}$, we have 
 \[
 \dim_F(Q\nu) > 0.
 \]

nodes.name: Proposition 10.1: Prop Fourier coefficients of restricted measures
Lemma 1.8: Lem Kahane's reduction to Fourier coefficients
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a  finite positive  Borel  measure on $[0,1]$.  Then 
\[
\dim_F(\mu)= \sup \{ D \in [0,1):    \text{$|\widehat{\mu}(n)|^2  = O(n^{-D})$ as $\mathbb{N} \ni n \to \infty$}    \}. 
\]
